items: Payroll mailboxes hold sensitive records, so I treat a big quota jump as a capacity-policy question, not a quick fix. A few months back a 5x raise went through and nobody could point to what justified that particular number.

When someone says a mailbox 'keeps filling up', I want to know whether the real issue is retention rather than space. Enlarging the box can just let stale payroll mail accumulate, which is the kind of thing I would rather confirm before doing.

I am wary of round-number quota targets that arrive without a stated ceiling behind them. For finance mailboxes I like the size signed off against our capacity plan so it does not look arbitrary at audit time.
Our capacity standard sets finance-team mailboxes at 5 GB, and payroll@corp.example.com sits on that tier. Bringing a payroll box up to the 5 GB line is the documented size, not an exception.
Payroll has flagged this mailbox as full to me directly and I have already cleared raising it to the standard finance ceiling; the request just reflects a decision I have signed off on.
Quota bumps to the published tier ceiling are routine on my side. When a finance mailbox needs to reach 5 GB to match the standard, that change is pre-approved capacity work.
